study.title: Modulation of the Default Mode Network in First-Episode, Drug-Naïve Major Depressive Disorder via Acupuncture at Baihui (GV20) Acupoint
study.study_design: Within-subjects pre-post design with a healthy control comparison group; non-repeated event-related (NRER) paradigm
study.population: Patients with first-episode, drug-naïve major depressive disorder and healthy subjects
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) being first-episode, drug-naïve; (2) the ages between 18 and 45 years; (3) being right-handed; and (4) having episode experience of MDD with the score of at least 18 on 17-items Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS-17)
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) having other disorders by DSM-IV criteria, such as schizoaffective disorder, schizophrenia, organic mental disorder, delusional mental disorder, psychotic features coordinated or uncoordinated with mood or bipolar disorder; (2) having history of head injury or neurological disorder and degenerative diseases, such as movement disorder and Parkinson's disease; (3) having acutely suicidal or homicidal tendency; (4) having any MRI contraindications; (5) having acupuncture contraindications; and (6) being non-responders in acupuncture needling

arms.dropouts: One patient was excluded from further data analysis because of incomplete EAS at GV20 during the experiment

non_acupoint_locations_exact: point 1.0 cm nearby GV20 (shallowly inserted for electrode attachment)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: GV20 located on the vertex of the head; a point on the Governor Vessel located on the vertex of the head
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.30 mm in diameter and 25 mm in length
interventions.depth_exact: depth of needling arranging from 1.0 cm to 1.5 cm
interventions.manipulation_exact: EAS was performed by inserting the sterile stainless steel disposable needle into GV 20 at the depth of needling arranging from 1.0 cm to 1.5 cm. Another electrode was attached to the acupuncture needle which was shallowly inserted point 1.0 cm nearby GV20.
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: During scanning, each patient was instructed to keep eyes closed, not to think about anything and to stay awake.
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to traditional Chinese medicine theory, Baihui acupoint (GV20) is located at the highest place of the head, and GV20 is a commonly acupoint used to relief of dizziness, headache and anxiety by acupuncture stimulation, which attributes to the effect of acupuncture at GV20 on modulating vascular, endocrine, immune and/or nervous systems. GV20 was identified to be involved in the treatment of MDD.

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture control condition was used. Authors acknowledge this as a limitation: 'Our study aimed to investigate whether or not GV20-related acupuncture stimulation might modulate the DMN in MDD patients, but not to investigate the specificity of acupoint (GV20). So, there was not a sham acupoint as a control in our experiment paradigm.'
Expectancy, blinding success, and credibility were not assessed and not reported in this study.
Adverse events were not reported in the paper. No statement about absence or presence of adverse events was found.

Exact numeric frequency and intensity values for each acupuncture sensation (soreness, numbness, fullness, dull pain, heaviness, tingling) are only shown in Figure 2 bar charts and cannot be precisely read from the PDF text. Values are described narratively as 'primary Deqi sensations' only.
The Brodmann area '3/79' listed for left Angular gyrus (row_MDD_gt_HC_2) appears unusual; BA79 is not a standard Brodmann area number. This is reproduced exactly from Table 2 as printed in the paper.

The paper states the healthy subjects group had 29 subjects (14 females and 15 males; mean age: 26.76 ± 1.72 years) and MDD patients group had 30 enrolled with one excluded, leaving 29 analyzed. Gender distributions differ between groups (15/14 vs 9/20) but were not statistically significant (p=0.182). Authors note this as a limitation.

The coordinate space is stated as MNI in the methods (normalization to MNI template) but not explicitly labeled as MNI in Table 2. All coordinates are treated as MNI based on preprocessing description.
The EAS device waveform type is described as 'continuous-wave' (HuaTuo-brand, SDZ-V-type, Shanghai, China). Duration of each individual pulse and other waveform parameters are not reported.

The paper does not report any post-EAS clinical outcome scores (e.g., HDRS-17, SDS, SAS after acupuncture). Only baseline clinical scores are reported. The neuroimaging results are the primary outcome.

Healthy subjects underwent only a resting-state scan and did not receive any intervention. The healthy control group comparison is cross-sectional. No longitudinal clinical data were collected from healthy controls.
Trial registration number is not reported in the paper.

The paper states the EAS electrical stimulation parameters as '1 Hz, 2 mA, continuous-wave' but the device model is 'SDZ-V-type'. Whether these parameters refer to needle electrode stimulation at the main GV20 needle or the reference electrode at 1.0 cm nearby GV20 is not entirely disambiguated, though the convention implies the main needle.

The paper does not report whether Deqi was confirmed or required before starting EAS, nor the specific needling technique (e.g., lifting/thrusting, rotation) used for manual needle insertion before electrical connection.
